args.body:
Hi Dora! 👋 Welcome to Slack — I just invited you and added you to #general.

I took a look at your personal website (www.dora-website.com) and wanted to share some feedback:

**What works:**
- It's clean and easy to load — no clutter, no pop-ups, no autoplay. That's a good foundation.
- The page tells the visitor right away what the site is (a personal site) and how to reach you (dora@gmail.com).

**Where I'd suggest improvements:**
- The site is very sparse right now — it's essentially one line of text. A personal site is a great chance to show personality, so consider adding a short intro about who you are and what you do.
- Add a few sections that are typical of personal sites: a bio, recent projects or work, a blog or notes, and links to your other profiles (LinkedIn, GitHub, etc.).
- Some visual polish would help — even a simple header image, a consistent color scheme, and readable typography would make it feel finished rather than like a placeholder.
- A "Contact" section with a small form (or a mailto link) would make it easier for people to reach out than just listing a bare email address.
- Make sure it looks good on mobile, since most visitors will arrive from a phone or a shared link.

Overall, a nice, no-nonsense starting point — it just needs a bit more content and personality to really shine. Happy to share more specific ideas if you'd like!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! 👋

I had a look at your blog (www.eve-blog.com) and wanted to share some feedback:

**What works:**
- The site is lightweight and loads instantly — a real plus for a blog.
- It immediately gives visitors a sense of who you are and what you're passionate about (hiking is a great topic, and it's the kind of thing that makes a blog feel personal and approachable).

**Where I'd suggest improvements:**
- Right now the blog is just a single line, so there's nothing for a reader to actually dig into. The biggest win would be adding a few real posts — even short ones about a trail you loved, gear you rely on, or a beginner's guide to something you enjoy.
- Add a homepage structure: a short welcome intro, a list of recent posts with dates, and maybe a "About" section.
- Since hiking is your thing, photos would be a huge asset. A simple gallery or image-rich post layout would make the blog much more engaging.
- Consider organizing posts by topic (e.g., trail guides, gear reviews, trip reports) so readers can find what they're interested in.
- Add a way for readers to subscribe — an RSS feed, a newsletter signup, or links to your social accounts — so people can come back for new posts.
- A search function and tags would be useful once the post count grows.
- Double-check mobile responsiveness and add a simple footer with contact info and social links.

Overall, a nice, fast foundation with a clear personal angle. With a handful of posts and some structure, it could become a really enjoyable hiking blog!

Best,
Emma Johnson
